flags.why: This word has a literary register that the untagged entry does not indicate.
The word describes clumsy or unsteady movement, rather than dawdling ([dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lo%E1%BA%A1ng_qu%E1%BA%A1ng)).
In whale-worship usage, luỵ means to die, rather than to become beached ([heritage source](https://hoianheritage.danang.gov.vn/uploads/download/files/ban-tin-2-2020.pdf)).
flags.fix: to die (of a whale, in whale-worship traditions)

flags.why: The example refers to a whale dying at the shore, which 'was beached' does not convey ([heritage source](https://hoianheritage.danang.gov.vn/uploads/download/files/ban-tin-2-2020.pdf)).
flags.fix: A whale died at the shore, and the whole village held a funeral for it.

flags.why: Quân giặc means enemy troops, whereas the translation reduces it to neutral 'soldiers'.
flags.fix: The enemy troops built a rampart to block their opponent's advance.

flags.why: Luỹ tiến means progressively increasing and does not specify exponential growth ([dictionary](https://www.thuvienlamdong.org.vn/Files/Books/53119.pdf)).

The supposed literal sense is an invented meaning of an idiom about satisfying many people's demands ([idiom dictionary](https://huyenbi.net/Tu-dien-Thanh-ngu-Tuc-ngu-Viet-Nam/Y-nghia-cua-tu-Lam-dau-tram-ho-1733.html)).
